newsitem.title: FRANCE: French airfreight hit by airline/trucker disputes.
newsitem.headline: French airfreight hit by airline/trucker disputes.

text.p: France's airfreight sector, already badly hit by strikes by the country's lorry drivers, is now having to cope with a two-day industrial action by airline staff.
Air France Cargo said it expected to have to cancel six out of 14 Boeing 747-200F flights scheduled to operate today and tomorrow.
Pilots and crews at several French airlines are going on strike to protest against deregulation in the European air industry and what it says is unfair competition.

"Frankly, today looks being hellish! Volumes are already down due to the road blocks and for the freight that does manage to get through there is a reduced number full-freighter flights in service while belly capacity is also being affected as a result of the cancellation of some long-haul passenger flights," a Charles de Gaulle(CDG)-based forwarder told Reuters.
Another forwarder said shippers were adopting a prudent approach to despatching goods since the lorry drivers action had been prolonged.
"There's been a tail-off in the normal volume of freight with shippers preferring to withhold shipments until the trucking situation improves."
He also warned of a possible long-term impact on traffic because of the dispute.

"We've had a hard job rebuilding the credibility of the Paris airports as major gateway for ex-Europe airfreight in the light of previous strikes in recent years. There's a real risk this latest dispute will give shippers fresh cause to use other gateways instead."

Road Flight Systems (RFS), a road haulage company specialising in trucking freight on behalf of several airlines, said its activities were at a near-standstill as a result of the French lorry drivers dispute.
"Only one of our 40-strong fleet of trucks is available at the moment, the remainder either being blocked in barricades or waiting to return to France from European," an RFS official told Reuters.
Air France Cargo said it was difficult to get a precise picture on the impact on trucking services.
"We can confirm that traffic to the UK is totally blocked," an airline official added.
Air France normally operates daily round trips between Paris and London while Manchester and Glasgow also feature on its trucking network.
"Serious problems were still reported in south-west France and several borders areas."

Some transporters were choosing to wait while others were attempting trucking runs in opting for alternative itineraries and for that reason, information was not easy to obtain on the degree to which services were being hit, the official said. - Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
